samples.marker_line: NTLM capture: coerces WebDAV and logs Type-3 authentication
trace: Creates an HttpListener at localhost:8080 and launches net use against the local WebDAV-style UNC path in a background job.
401 challenges negotiate NTLM; the Base64 constant decodes to a 48-byte NTLMSSP Type-2 message, flags 0x8201 and nonce 1122334455667788.
Decodes incoming NTLM Authorization values; byte 8 selects Type 1 challenge responses and Type 3 authentication messages. Appends full Type-3 headers to TEMP/handshakes.log until four are recorded.

Actual local credential capture tips the malicious judgment. Authorized assessment context is absent. Loopback-only networking does not establish relay, privilege escalation or exfiltration; Windows WebClient and authentication policy affect success.

samples.marker_line: Browser tasking: hidden commands, output upload and reverse SSH
trace: Force-kills Edge and deletes wildcard partial download files. Launches Edge in a 1x1 window at coordinates 10000,10000 with certificate errors ignored.
Decoded Base64 HTML fetches a webhook.site response, converts it to a Blob and clicks an anchor to save a .000 file. The batch copies Downloads/*.000 to TEMP/stage.cmd after five seconds.
cmd /c executes stage.cmd and captures stdout and stderr in result.txt. curl --data-binary sends that same result path to the webhook endpoint; the staged script and output file are then deleted.

Downloads an SSH identity under ProgramData/Adobe, changes owner and ACL, and invokes in-box OpenSSH with that identity, disabled host-key checking and an unattended remote dynamic forward (-R address:port -Nf) to root at a fixed public address on port 80.

Concealed remote command acquisition, execution and output callback tip the malicious judgment. No authorized deployment context was supplied. There is one fetch, no polling loop, no proven reboot persistence and no recovered remote command body. CORS, download timing, directory existence, WebClient/SSH configuration and remote availability are not tested.

samples.marker_line: Parser probe: inert example request; retain bypass-pattern traits
trace: Assigns an HTTP POST request here-string, then calls Text.Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes on it. The only result is a local byte array; there is no network client, send, file write, process creation, evaluator or embedded second stage.
The request combines an empty semicolon path parameter, Forwarded for="127.0.0.\1", a SOAPAction and a CreatePrivilegedSession body: the access-control parser-differential attack shape is real.

Product-neutral construction, an appliance.example target, a stale Content-Length of 114 for a 135-byte body, and the absence of any use of the byte array together support a benign exploit/request fixture. Lack of a sender alone would not establish benign intent.

Retains the suspicious escaped-loopback observation and both hostile exploit-pattern findings. Their descriptions now describe the request shape and SOAPAction header without claiming a successful bypass or contact with a service. Deployment context and intended consuming harness remain unavailable.

changes.test_expectations: Two pre-existing NTLM positive controls required a hostile capture finding but capped maximum criticality at suspicious. Corrected only those maxima to hostile; negative and coercion-only limits remain unchanged.
changes.placement_contract: TAXONOMY.md defines shell/script-file by a required script operand, distinguishing command text, pipelines and stream setup without script invocation. Both output-capturing and plain script launches belong to this command form. No budget was increased and neither full destination directory was split.

consumer_audit.effective_rule_equality: Compared each relocated trait plus inherited defaults against git HEAD: matcher, exclusions, confidence, criticality, platform and type scopes are byte/value-equivalent.
consumer_audit.exact_consumers: Updated batch-script-execution, service-temp-batch-command-dispatch, batch-command-output-browser-form-exfil and windows-process-watchdog-loop.
consumer_audit.directory_consumers: All three moved traits retain their process/create membership (for script launch and output-capturing script launch) or move generic timeout out of lifecycle supervision into sleep. No exact directory consumer selects the old script/file or lifecycle/supervise leaves. Audited shell ancestor consumers: the two relocated traits require shell/script-file command forms. The only time/sleep objective consumer is PowerShell-scoped and cannot gain the timeout atom, whose scope excludes PowerShell.
consumer_audit.source_disposition: Unrelated rules in both legacy source directories remain in place; this is a targeted relocation of the firing observations, not retirement of either directory.

verification.browser_fixture_comparison: All eight positive/near-miss artifacts retain every prior finding at the same criticality after applying the relocation mapping.
verification.scanner_note: Installed atomscan uses an older Cleave taxonomy budget and fails startup validation on the already-reviewed metadata/file/naming budget of 101. For before/after scans only, CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 allowed unchanged rule evaluation. Final validation uses the available newer Cleave binary, which admits this documented budget.
verification.archives: The inputs are individual text files. No archive members exist. Base64 HTML and NTLM challenge bytes were independently decoded; the HTML is also represented in cleave facts and scanner decoded-layer observations.
verification.validation_iteration: Initial validation rejected inserting into command-mode and fd/stdio, both already at 100 rules, and found two redundant scope fields. The required script-file command form now has its precise documented leaf; redundant scope fields were removed without changing effective scopes.
verification.model_compatibility_note: Final atomscan runs warn that the model uses feature specification v18 while the extractor expects v19; newer feature fields are filled with zero for compatibility. The complete rule findings and calibrated classifications were compared; verdicts are based on code behavior rather than these scores.

remaining_disagreements: NTLM is judged MALICIOUS but calibrated ML remains benign; accurate hostile credential capture and suspicious coercion findings are retained.
The parser request fixture is judged BENIGN while two hostile exploit-pattern traits remain accurate observations of its attack-shaped content. Calibrated ML is benign.
coverage_gap: NTLM supports one hostile capture result and one suspicious coercion observation. No second independent hostile outcome is evidenced; relay, cracking, privilege escalation and exfiltration must not be invented to reach a trait count.
